# Zero Dependency, No Build Step

Wherever a dependency can be replaced by code, it is. Wherever a build step can be avoided, it is.
Confirmed across eight repositories — but the honest version of this pattern is that it holds at
**module** level far more consistently than at repo level.

## The pure cases

- `Information-Systems-Modelling/lab6/app/package.json` declares `"dependencies": {}` and serves over
  `node:http`; `lab7/package.json` has **no `dependencies` key at all**.
- `Python-Programming-Laboratories`' core `weblog` package declares `dependencies = []`, pushing
  every library to an optional `labs` extra.
- `Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories/lab4_Complexity/part2` and `lab6_Neo4j/viewer/` contain **zero**
  external URLs.
- `Optimization Methods`' entire C++17 solver is standard-library only — no Boost, no LEMON, no
  OR-Tools, no LP/MIP solver anywhere.

> "No build step. No server. No internet. **Open one HTML file and start revising.**"
> — Physics/README.md, 2026-07-10

> "# Only the later laboratories need these; the core package has no dependencies."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/pyproject.toml, 2026-07-25

## Vendoring over CDNs — and the internal contradiction

`Physics` copies KaTeX in wholesale (css + js + 20 `.woff2`) specifically to avoid a CDN — see
[[vendor-katex-instead-of-cdn]]. `Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories` vendored React's production UMD
and precompiled its JSX after a CDN dependency broke `file://` loading entirely — see
[[vendor-react-over-babel-cdn]].

But the same repo, in the sibling directory, does the opposite and says so:

> "No dependencies are vendored; there is nothing to `npm install`."
> — Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories/lab5_GraphTheory/Q-HYDRO Wrocław/README.md, 2026-06-09

Q-HYDRO loads Leaflet 1.9.4, map tiles and IBM Plex from CDNs. **Two lab-5 apps sit side by side
under opposite rules**, and the root README's claim that labs 4 (part 2), 5 and 6 "all run offline"
overstates it. `Optimization Methods` and `Information-Systems-Modelling` show the same split —
zero-dependency Node tooling next to CDN-loaded Leaflet and Google Fonts.

## The deeper form: refuse the asset pipeline

`browser_game_stickfps` has 12 runtime dependencies and two build pipelines, so it contradicts this
pattern at the toolchain level. One layer down it applies the same instinct absolutely:

> "**If a design needs an asset, it must be procedurally generatable in code, or it's out.**"
> — browser_game_stickfps/DESIGN_PROMPT.md, 2026-07-25

All geometry from three.js primitives, all sound synthesized in Web Audio, textures as inline-SVG
data URIs. See [[no-external-assets]]. `Farley` shows the same at module level inside a ~40-dependency
shell: a "zero-dep IndexedDB" diagnostics store, an offline built-in car dataset, a calendar computed
with no library, and a LITE tier that replaces MapLibre with hand-rolled DOM/SVG projection.

So the accurate statement of the pattern is narrower than "no dependencies": **replace a dependency
with code wherever the replacement is small enough to own.**
